outlines.a: Committee A copies B standing to claim chair authority; B needs to explain standing was a cramp. Apology dispute becomes whether B must stand to address chair.
outlines.b: A copies a training whistle incorrectly; B wants safe drill and offers apology to trainees. A needs apology timed before next direction, not merely drill sympathy.

outlines.a: A copies voice-note gesture as endorsement recording; B actually timing speech and wants written rota comments. A recruits visible emailed endorsement.
outlines.b: A copies penciled marks on extension plan as supporting signatures; B only measured. A needs attributable support; B offers conditional initials.

outlines.a: A copies rolled sleeves as promotion insignia, assigns B washing after event. B explains practical sleeve use and late plumber; A invents rank permitting lockup.
outlines.b: A copies inspector initials as approval before learning receipt-only. A puts B below A as complaints officer; B hearing burden drives delegated signature.

outlines.a: A copies raised hand as booking authorization; B was asking a question. A conceals ignorance by probing who authorizes deposit while B needs coach booked.
outlines.b: A copies stamp without knowing receipt versus release. B needs leak fixed and reveals finance/caretaker precedent. A probes true reversal power.

outlines.a: A copies raised keys as a shed-vote signal; B was looking for lost key owner. A uses correction to recruit access advocates.
outlines.b: A copies morning-class name list as supporters but it is attendance. B offers weekend concern, allowing A to build real cross-class coalition.
